plan.title: Your plan
plan.empty: No plan yet. Take the quiz to build your personal training plan.

hrZones.title: Heart rate zones
hrZones.description: Your five training zones from max, resting or threshold heart rate.

methodInfo.percentMax: Zones as a percentage of your maximum heart rate. Simple and a good start.
methodInfo.karvonen: Uses your heart rate reserve (max minus resting). More personal, because it reflects your fitness.
methodInfo.lthr: Zones from your lactate threshold heart rate (Joe Friel). The most precise if you know your threshold.

hrZones.autoMethod: Chosen automatically: Karvonen as soon as you enter your resting heart rate.
hrZones.hrMaxEstimateNote: Estimated from your age (208 − 0.7 × age). A measured value makes your zones more accurate.

zone2.title: Zone 2 calculator
zone2.description: Find your easy aerobic range – and why it matters.

benefits.base: Builds your aerobic base: more mitochondria and capillaries, so you get faster at the same heart rate.
benefits.fat: Trains your body to burn fat efficiently, which saves carbohydrates for hard efforts.
benefits.recovery: Easy enough to recover from quickly, so you can train more often without getting injured.
benefits.volume: Most endurance athletes do around 80 % of their training at this easy intensity.

zone2.restingHint: With resting heart rate the Karvonen method is used – more personal.

methodNote.percentMax: 60–70 % of your max heart rate ({{hrMax}} bpm).
methodNote.karvonen: 60–70 % of your heart rate reserve (Karvonen, max {{hrMax}} bpm).
methodNote.lthr: Based on your threshold heart rate.

zone2.talkTest: Check: you can still talk in full sentences. If not, slow down.

pace.title: Pace & race predictor
pace.description: Training paces and predicted race times from a recent race.
pace.intro: Enter a recent race or all-out time trial. The more recent, the better.
pace.thresholdNote: About the pace you could hold for one hour.
pace.predictionsNote: Riegel formula. Assumes you train for the distance – longer races, especially the marathon, are often slower than predicted.

swim.title: Swim pace (CSS)
swim.description: Critical Swim Speed and swim zones per 100 m from a simple test.
swim.guideTitle: How to do the CSS test

guide.warmUp: Warm up for 10–15 minutes with easy swimming and a few short pick-ups.
guide.swim400: Swim 400 m as fast as you can at an even pace. Note the time.
guide.recover: Recover for 5–10 minutes with very easy swimming.
guide.swim200: Swim 200 m all-out. Note the time.
guide.record: Use the same pool and push-off starts for both efforts, then enter both times below.

swim.cssNote: Roughly the pace you can sustain for about 30 minutes.

fields.ageHint: Used to estimate your max heart rate if you don't know it.
fields.hrMaxHint: Highest heart rate you have measured, e.g. at the end of an all-out effort.
fields.hrMaxLthrHint: Sets the top of zone 5. Leave empty if unknown.
fields.restingHrHint: Measure in the morning before getting up.
fields.lthrHint: Average heart rate over the last 20 minutes of a 30-minute all-out solo run.

validation.invalidDuration: Minutes and seconds must be below 60.
validation.ageOrHrMaxRequired: Enter your age or your max heart rate.
validation.restingHrNotBelowHrMax: Resting heart rate must be below your max heart rate ({{hrMax}} bpm).
validation.lthrNotBelowHrMax: Threshold heart rate must be below your max heart rate ({{hrMax}} bpm).
validation.unrealisticRaceTime: This time looks unrealistic for the distance. Enter a time between {{min}} and {{max}}.
validation.swim400NotSlowerThan200: Your 400 m pace must be slower than your 200 m pace. Please check both times.
validation.swimTimesInconsistent: These times are very far apart. Were both swims all-out efforts?
validation.targetNotAfterStart: The target date must be after the start date.
validation.planTooLong: Plans can be at most {{max}} weeks long. Choose an earlier target date.
validation.goalNeedsSports: This goal needs all of its disciplines – for a triathlon swim, bike and run.
validation.notEnoughAvailability: Plan at least 2 days with 20 minutes or more.
validation.underageWeightLoss: The weight-loss goal is only available from age {{min}}.

run.recovery: Very easy running helps your legs recover from the last hard session.
run.easy: Easy Zone 2 running builds your aerobic engine – the base of every plan.
run.easyStrides: An easy run with a few short, relaxed strides keeps your legs quick without tiring you.
run.long: The long run builds endurance and teaches your body to run efficiently for longer.
run.uphillHike: Steep hiking and running builds the climbing strength mountain events demand.
run.progression: Starting easy and finishing faster teaches pacing and builds fitness without a hard interval session.
run.fartlek: Playful surges by feel – a gentle introduction to faster running that works on any terrain.
run.hillsShort: Short hill sprints build power and running economy with low injury risk.
run.hillsLong: Longer hill repeats build strength endurance at threshold effort.
run.tempo: Threshold running raises the pace you can hold for a long time.
run.vo2: Intervals at VO2max pace raise your aerobic ceiling.
run.racePace: Running at goal race pace makes that pace feel familiar and controlled on race day.
run.downhill: Controlled descents prepare your legs for the eccentric load of downhill racing.

bike.recovery: An easy spin with high cadence flushes your legs after hard days.
bike.endurance: Steady Zone 2 riding builds aerobic fitness with little fatigue.
bike.long: The long ride builds the endurance you need for long days in the saddle.
bike.commute: Your commute counts as easy training – it is part of the plan.
bike.tempo: Steady tempo efforts build muscular endurance.
bike.sweetspot: Sweet-spot intervals give a lot of fitness for the time invested.
bike.threshold: Threshold intervals raise the power you can sustain for an hour.
bike.vo2: Short, hard intervals raise your maximum aerobic power.
bike.climb: Climbing efforts build strength on the bike and prepare you for hilly routes.
bike.cadence: Cadence drills improve pedalling efficiency inside an easy ride.

swim.technique: Drills improve your stroke – in swimming, technique is the fastest way to get faster.
swim.aerobic: Steady aerobic swimming builds endurance in the water.
swim.easy: Easy continuous swimming keeps the feel for the water without extra fatigue.
swim.css: Repeats at your Critical Swim Speed raise the pace you can hold over distance.
swim.speed: Short fast repeats with long rest build speed and a strong stroke.
swim.openwater: Sighting and continuous swimming prepare you for open-water racing.

why.brick: Running straight off the bike teaches your legs the transition you will feel on race day.

winter.xcski: Cross-country skiing builds the same aerobic fitness – with less impact on your legs.
winter.xcskiIntervals: Intervals on skis train your threshold while giving your running legs a break.
winter.skitour: Ski touring builds climbing endurance; the ascent is the training.
winter.snowshoe: Snowshoeing is a low-impact, full-body endurance session.

benchmark.run5k: A 5 km time trial updates your pace zones and race prediction.
benchmark.run30: A 30-minute solo effort measures your threshold heart rate (average of the last 20 minutes).
benchmark.swimCss: A 400 m and 200 m time trial updates your Critical Swim Speed.
benchmark.bikeFtp: A 20-minute test estimates your FTP (about 95 % of the average power).

strength.peakrBase: General strength now makes you more robust for the harder endurance weeks ahead.
strength.peakrBuild: Heavy, low-rep strength and jumps make you more economical and powerful.
strength.peakrPeak: A short maintenance session keeps your strength while the endurance work peaks.
strength.coreMobility: Core and mobility work keeps you moving well without tiring your legs.
strength.fullBody: A full-body session from your split.
strength.upper: Upper-body work from your split – it does not tire your legs for running or riding.
strength.legs: Leg day from your split, placed so it does not hurt your key endurance sessions.
strength.runners: Runner-specific strength for hips, calves and single-leg stability.
strength.routine: Your own routine, placed so it fits around the endurance sessions.

notes.benchmark: Test week: this session updates your zones.
notes.downgraded: Planned {{type}} session made easy – it did not fit your available time without two hard days in a row.
notes.intensityBalance: Planned {{type}} session made easy to keep about 80 % of your training easy.
notes.loadCap: Shortened so this week does not increase the training load by more than 10 %.
notes.loadCapEasy: Planned {{type}} session made shorter and easy so this week does not increase the load by more than 10 %.
notes.recoveryWeek: Recovery week – less load so your body can absorb the training.
notes.taperWeek: Taper – less volume, some sharpness, fresh legs for race day.
notes.shortPreparation: Only {{weeks}} weeks until your race – {{recommended}} weeks are recommended, so the plan is compressed.
notes.strengthMerged: Not enough free days for your split: sessions are combined into {{sessions}}.
notes.strengthNoDay: No free day for strength this week.
notes.strengthSkipped: The {{type}} strength session did not fit this week without hurting a key session.

steps.lthrWindow: Average heart rate of this part = threshold heart rate
steps.timeTrial: Time trial – all out, evenly paced

back_squat.name: Back squat
back_squat.howTo: Bar on your upper back, feet shoulder-width. Sit down between your heels until your thighs are at least parallel, chest up, knees tracking over your toes. Drive up through the whole foot.

front_squat.name: Front squat
front_squat.howTo: Bar resting on the front of your shoulders, elbows high. Squat straight down keeping your torso upright, then stand up without letting the elbows drop.

goblet_squat.name: Goblet squat
goblet_squat.howTo: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell at your chest. Squat down between your knees, elbows inside the knees, chest tall, then stand up.

leg_press.name: Leg press
leg_press.howTo: Feet hip-width in the middle of the platform. Lower until your knees are at about 90°, keep your lower back on the pad, press back up without locking the knees.

bodyweight_squat.name: Bodyweight squat
bodyweight_squat.howTo: Feet shoulder-width, arms forward for balance. Sit back and down as deep as you can with a flat back, then stand up tall.

split_squat.name: Split squat
split_squat.howTo: Long stride stance. Lower the back knee straight down towards the floor, front shin roughly vertical, then push up through the front foot. Switch legs after the set.

bulgarian_split_squat.name: Bulgarian split squat
bulgarian_split_squat.howTo: Rear foot on a bench behind you. Lower until the front thigh is about parallel, torso slightly forward, then drive up through the front heel.

deadlift.name: Deadlift
deadlift.howTo: Bar over mid-foot, hip-width stance. Hinge to grip the bar, flat back, shoulders over the bar. Push the floor away and stand up tall, then lower with control.

romanian_deadlift.name: Romanian deadlift
romanian_deadlift.howTo: Stand tall with the weight. Push your hips back with soft knees, sliding the weight down your thighs until you feel the hamstrings stretch, then drive the hips forward.

single_leg_rdl.name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
single_leg_rdl.howTo: Stand on one leg. Hinge forward while the free leg reaches back, hips square, back flat. Return to standing by squeezing the glute of the standing leg.

hip_thrust.name: Hip thrust
hip_thrust.howTo: Upper back on a bench, weight across your hips, feet flat. Drive the hips up until your body is straight from shoulders to knees, pause, lower with control.

glute_bridge.name: Glute bridge
glute_bridge.howTo: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Press through your heels and lift the hips until shoulders, hips and knees line up, squeeze, then lower.

kettlebell_swing.name: Kettlebell swing
kettlebell_swing.howTo: Hike the bell back between your legs, then snap the hips forward to float it to chest height. Power comes from the hips, not the arms.

good_morning.name: Good morning
good_morning.howTo: Bar on your upper back, soft knees. Push the hips back and lower your torso with a flat back until you feel the hamstrings, then return to standing.

walking_lunge.name: Walking lunge
walking_lunge.howTo: Step forward into a lunge, back knee close to the floor, then step through into the next lunge with the other leg. Keep your torso upright.

reverse_lunge.name: Reverse lunge
reverse_lunge.howTo: Step one foot back and lower the back knee towards the floor. Push through the front foot to return. Alternate legs or finish one side first.

step_up.name: Step-up
step_up.howTo: Place one foot fully on a box or bench. Drive through that foot to stand up on top without pushing off the back leg, then step down slowly.

lateral_lunge.name: Lateral lunge
lateral_lunge.howTo: Take a wide step to the side and sit into that hip, keeping the other leg straight and both feet flat. Push back to the start.

pistol_squat_progression.name: Pistol squat progression
pistol_squat_progression.howTo: Stand on one leg, the other leg forward. Squat down as far as you control – to a box or holding a support at first – then stand up.

standing_calf_raise.name: Standing calf raise
standing_calf_raise.howTo: Balls of your feet on a step. Rise as high as you can, pause, then lower the heels slowly below the step.

bent_knee_calf_raise.name: Bent-knee calf raise
bent_knee_calf_raise.howTo: Same as a calf raise but with the knees bent about 30°, which targets the soleus – important for runners.

tibialis_raise.name: Tibialis raise
tibialis_raise.howTo: Lean your back against a wall, heels about a foot away. Lift your toes as high as you can, then lower slowly.

single_leg_hops.name: Single-leg hops in place
single_leg_hops.howTo: Small, quick hops on one foot staying on the ball of the foot, knee slightly bent. Stay springy and quiet.

bench_press.name: Bench press
bench_press.howTo: Lie on the bench, eyes under the bar, shoulder blades squeezed together. Lower the bar to mid-chest with control, then press it back up.

dumbbell_press.name: Dumbbell press
dumbbell_press.howTo: Lie on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand above your chest. Lower them to chest level, elbows at about 45°, then press up.

incline_press.name: Incline press
incline_press.howTo: Bench set to 30–45°. Lower the weight to your upper chest and press it back up over your shoulders.

push_up.name: Push-up
push_up.howTo: Hands slightly wider than shoulders, body in a straight line. Lower your chest to just above the floor, then push back up.

feet_elevated_push_up.name: Feet-elevated push-up
feet_elevated_push_up.howTo: Like a push-up with your feet on a bench or chair. Keep the body straight and lower your chest towards the floor.

archer_push_up.name: Archer push-up
archer_push_up.howTo: Very wide hands. Lower towards one hand while the other arm stays almost straight, push back up and alternate sides.

dips.name: Dips
dips.howTo: Support yourself on parallel bars or a sturdy bench. Lower until your shoulders are just below the elbows, then press back up.

overhead_press.name: Overhead press
overhead_press.howTo: Bar on the front of your shoulders, glutes and core tight. Press straight overhead, moving your head back slightly, finish with arms locked.

dumbbell_shoulder_press.name: Dumbbell shoulder press
dumbbell_shoulder_press.howTo: Seated or standing, dumbbells at shoulder height. Press them overhead until the arms are straight, then lower with control.

pike_push_up.name: Pike push-up
pike_push_up.howTo: Hips high in an inverted V. Bend the elbows to lower the top of your head towards the floor, then push back up.

lateral_raise.name: Lateral raise
lateral_raise.howTo: Light dumbbells at your sides. Raise them out to shoulder height with slightly bent elbows, then lower slowly.

barbell_row.name: Barbell row
barbell_row.howTo: Hinge forward with a flat back. Pull the bar to your lower ribs, squeezing the shoulder blades, then lower with control.

dumbbell_row.name: Dumbbell row
dumbbell_row.howTo: One hand and knee on a bench. Pull the dumbbell towards your hip, elbow close to the body, then lower fully.

seated_cable_row.name: Seated cable row
seated_cable_row.howTo: Sit tall with a slight knee bend. Pull the handle to your stomach, shoulders down and back, then let the arms extend slowly.

inverted_row.name: Inverted row
inverted_row.howTo: Hang under a bar or sturdy table, body straight, heels on the floor. Pull your chest to the bar, then lower with control.

face_pull.name: Face pull
face_pull.howTo: Rope or band at face height. Pull towards your forehead, elbows high and wide, then return slowly.

pull_up.name: Pull-up
pull_up.howTo: Hang with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders. Pull your chest towards the bar, then lower all the way with control.

chin_up.name: Chin-up
chin_up.howTo: Like a pull-up with palms facing you and hands shoulder-width. Pull your chin over the bar.

lat_pulldown.name: Lat pulldown
lat_pulldown.howTo: Sit with thighs under the pad. Pull the bar to your upper chest, leading with the elbows, then let it rise slowly.

band_assisted_pull_up.name: Band-assisted pull-up
band_assisted_pull_up.howTo: Loop a band over the bar and put a knee or foot in it. Do pull-ups with the band's help; use lighter bands as you get stronger.

biceps_curl.name: Biceps curl
biceps_curl.howTo: Elbows by your sides. Curl the weight up without swinging, squeeze, then lower slowly.

hammer_curl.name: Hammer curl
hammer_curl.howTo: Like a biceps curl with palms facing each other throughout.

triceps_pushdown.name: Triceps pushdown
triceps_pushdown.howTo: At a cable station, elbows pinned to your sides. Push the bar or rope down until the arms are straight, then let it rise.

overhead_triceps_extension.name: Overhead triceps extension
overhead_triceps_extension.howTo: Hold one weight overhead with both hands. Lower it behind your head by bending the elbows, then extend back up.

plank.name: Plank
plank.howTo: Forearms under your shoulders, body straight from head to heels. Brace your stomach and hold without letting the hips sag.

side_plank.name: Side plank
side_plank.howTo: On one forearm, feet stacked. Lift the hips so your body forms a straight line and hold. Switch sides.

dead_bug.name: Dead bug
dead_bug.howTo: On your back, arms up, knees over hips. Slowly lower the opposite arm and leg while keeping your lower back on the floor, then switch.

bird_dog.name: Bird dog
bird_dog.howTo: On hands and knees, reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until straight. Hold briefly, keep the hips level, switch sides.

pallof_press.name: Pallof press
pallof_press.howTo: Stand side-on to a cable or band at chest height. Press the handle straight out and resist the pull to rotate, then bring it back.

hanging_knee_raise.name: Hanging knee raise
hanging_knee_raise.howTo: Hang from a bar. Raise your knees towards your chest without swinging, then lower slowly.

copenhagen_plank.name: Copenhagen plank
copenhagen_plank.howTo: Side plank with the top leg on a bench and the bottom leg free. Hold the hips up – a strong exercise for the adductors.

ab_wheel.name: Ab wheel rollout
ab_wheel.howTo: Kneel holding the wheel. Roll forward as far as you can keep your back flat, then pull back using your core.

pogo_hops.name: Pogo hops
pogo_hops.howTo: Quick, small two-footed jumps on the balls of your feet with stiff ankles, minimal ground contact time.

box_jump.name: Box jump
box_jump.howTo: Swing your arms and jump onto a box, landing softly in a quarter squat. Step down – don't jump down.

broad_jump.name: Broad jump
broad_jump.howTo: Swing your arms and jump forward as far as you can, landing softly on both feet. Reset before each jump.

bounding.name: Bounding
bounding.howTo: Exaggerated running strides: drive the knee up and push off powerfully, spending as long as possible in the air.

a_skips.name: A-skips
a_skips.howTo: Skip forward lifting one knee to hip height while the other foot strikes the ground under your hips. Rhythmic and light.

hip_flexor_stretch.name: Hip flexor stretch
hip_flexor_stretch.howTo: Half-kneeling, tuck your pelvis and shift forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the back hip. Hold, then switch.

ankle_dorsiflexion.name: Ankle dorsiflexion
ankle_dorsiflexion.howTo: Half-kneeling facing a wall. Drive the front knee towards the wall without lifting the heel, then return.

thoracic_rotation.name: Thoracic rotation
thoracic_rotation.howTo: On all fours, one hand behind your head. Rotate the elbow down and then up towards the ceiling, following it with your eyes.

hips_90_90.name: 90/90 hips
hips_90_90.howTo: Sit with both knees bent at 90°, one in front, one to the side. Rotate the knees to the other side without using your hands.

hamstring_floss.name: Hamstring floss
hamstring_floss.howTo: Lie on your back holding one leg behind the thigh. Straighten and bend the knee slowly while pointing and flexing the foot.
